spans.s:
mfn. (-तः-ता-तं)
White.
m. (-तः)
1 White, (the colour.)
2 The planet VENUS, or its regent Ś

UKRA.
3
The sixth range of mountains, dividing the known continent, the white mountains separating the Varṣas of Hiraṇmaya and

Romanaka.
4
One of the minor Dvīpas or divisions of the world; in fable the White Island, identified geographically by WILFORD, with

Britain.
5

A white cloud.
6

Cumminseed.
7

A conch.
mf. (-तः-ता)
A small white shell used as a coin, a Cowri.
n. (-तं)
Silver.
f. (-ता)
1 A grass, (Andropogon aciculatum.)
2 A plant, Kāṣṭha Pātāla (?)
3 A flower, (Clitoria ternatea.)
4

Hogweed.
5

Bent grass with white blossoms.
6 Bambu manna.
7

Crystal.
8

Clayed or candied sugar.
E.
श्वित to be white, aff. अच् or घञ्.

m. (-कः)
A Cowri.
n. (-कं)
Silver.
E.
कन् added to the preceding.

m. (-रः)
INDRA'S elephant.
E.
श्वेत white, and कुञ्जर an elephant.

m. (-तुः)
A Bauddha or Jaina saint.
E.
श्वेत white, and केतु a banner.

m. (-शः)
A variety of the Hyperanthera morunga.
E.
श्वेत white, and केश a filament.

n. (-लः)
The Saphara fish, (Cyprinus Sophore, HAM.)

m. (-रः)
A white variety of the Mimosa catechu.
E.
श्वेत, and खदिर the Khayar.

m. (-जः)
1 A white elephant.
2 The elephant of INDRA.
E.
श्वेत white, and गज an elephant.

m. (-रुत्)
A goose.
E.
श्वेत white, and गरुत् a wing.

m. (-दः)
1 A goose.
2 A kind of basil, (Ocymum album, &c.)
E.
श्वेत white, and छद a feather or leaf.

n. (-णं)
White or refined borax.
E.
श्वेत white, and टङ्कण the same.

f. (-र्व्वा)
A bent grass with white blossoms.
E.
श्वेत, and टूर्व्वा Doob grass.

m. (-पः)
1 A white elephant.
2 INDRA'S elephant.
E.
श्वेत white, and द्विप an elephant.

m. (-पः)
The white island, or a minor division of the universe so called: also termed Candra Dvīpa, and supposed by WILFORD to be Britain.
E.
श्वेत white, and द्वीप an island; also श्वेत q. v.

Chalk.
2

The milk stone, opal or chalcedony.
E.
श्वेत white, घातु a mineral.

m. (-मा)
1 The moon.
2

Camphor.
3

Cuttle fish bone.
E.
श्वेत white, and धामन् a ray.

m. (-लः)
A cloud.
E.
श्वेत white, and नील black or dark blue.

m. (-त्रः)
A goose.
E.
श्वेत white, and पत्र a feather.

m. (-थः)
BRAHMĀ.
E.
श्वेतपत्र a goose, and रथ a car or conveyance.

n. (-द्मं)
The white lotus.
E.
श्वेत white, and पद्म a lotus.

m. (-सः)
Holy basil, or a variety of it, (Ocymum sanctum or album).
E.
श्वेत white, and पर्णास the same.

f. (-ला)
Trumpet flower, (Bignonia suave-olens.)
E.
श्वेत white, and पाटला the same.

m. (-ङ्गः)
A lion.
E.
श्वेत white, and पिङ्ग tawny; of a light tawny colour.

m. (-लः)
A lion.
E.
श्वेत white, and पिङ्गल tawny; see the last; also with कन् added, श्वेतपिङ्गलक.

m. (-ष्पः)
A plant, (Vitex trifolia.)
f. (-ष्पा)
A Ghoṣa with white flowers.
E.
श्वेत white, and पुष्प a flower.

m. (-कः)
A plant, (Nerium odorum, the white variety.)
E.
कन् added to the last.

m. (-कः)
A tree, (Tapia cratæva.)
E.
श्वेत white, (flowers,) प्रसूनक productive.

f. (-ण्डा)
A flower, (Clitoria ternatea.)

n. (-चं)
The seed of the Hyperanthera morunga.
E.
श्वेत white, and मरिच pepper.

m. (-क्तः)
Pale red or pink, (the colour.)
E.
श्वेत white, and रक्त red.

m. (-थः)
The planet VENUS.
E.
श्वेत white, and रथ a car.

n. (-नं)
Lead.
E.
श्वेत white, रञ्जन colouring.

f. (-स्ना)
A plant, white Rasan: see रास्ना.

m. (-चिः)
The moon.
E.
श्वेत white, and रोचिस् light.

m. (-तः)
GARUḌA.
E.
श्वेत white, and रोहित red.

f. (-चा)
Orris root, (Acorus calamus.)
E.
श्वेत white, and वचा the same.

m. (-लः)
Glomerous fig tree, (Ficus glomerata.)
E.
श्वेत white, and वल्कल bark.

m. (-जी)
1 The moon.
2 The prince ARJUNA.
E.
श्वेत white, वाजि a horse, इनि aff.

m. (-साः)
A religious mendicant, wearing white garments.
E.
श्वेत, and वासस् vesture.

m. (-हः)
ARJUNA.
E.
श्वेत white, and वाह a horse.

m. (-नः)
1 The moon.
2

ARJUNA.
3

The Makara, a marine monster.
E.
श्वेत white, and वाहन a vehicle.

m. (-ही)
ARJUNA.
E.
श्वेत white, and वाह a vehicle, (a horse,) इनि aff.

m. (-ङ्गः)
Barley.
E.
श्वेत white, and शुङ्ग awn.

m. (-र्पः)
1 A tree, (Tapia cratæva.)
2 A white snake.
E.
श्वेत white, सर्प what creeps or grows, or a serpent.

m. (-रः)
A tree, (Mimosa catechu)
E.
श्वेत white, सार pith or essence.

f. (-सा)
A white variety of the Nyctanthes arbor-tristis.
E.
श्वेत white, and सुरसा the Rasan, &c. to which it is compared.

m. (-यः)
1 A white horse.
2 The horse of

INDRA.
3

A name of ARJUNA.
E.
श्वेत white, and हय a horse.

m. (-स्ती)
1 A white elephant.
2 The elephant of INDRA.
E.
श्वेत white, and हस्तिन् an elephant.

m. (-र्कः)
Gigantic swallow-wort, (Asclepias gigantea,) with white flowers.
E.
श्वेत white, and अर्क the same.

m. (-रः)
KUVERA.
E.
श्वेत white, and उदर the belly.

f. (-च्छा)
Wilfulness, following one's own purpose or inclination.
E.
स्व own, इच्छा wish.

m. (-त्युः)
BHĪṢMA.
E.
स्वेच्छा wish, and मृत्यु death.

mfn. (-रः-रा-रं)
Omnivorous, eating anything at pleasure.
E.
स्वेच्छा, and आहार food.

mfn. (-दः-दा-दं)
Warm, perspiring.
m. (-दः)
1 Warmth, heat.
2 Perspiration, sweat.
3 Warm vapour, steam.
E.
ष्विद to perspire, &c, aff. घञ्.

m. (-कः)
A pleasant and cooling breeze.
E.
स्वेद perspiration, चूष to suck or imbibe, aff. वुन्.

mfn. (-छित्)
Cooling, allaying perspiration.
E.
स्वेद, and छिद् what cuts.

mfn. (-जः-जा-जं)
Engendered by heat and damp, as insects and worms.
E.
स्वेद sweat or warm vapour, and ज produced.

n. (-लं)
Perspiration.
E.
स्वेद, and जल water.

n. (-नं)
1 Perspiration, sweat.
2 Sweeting, causing to perspire.
3 A diaphoretic, a sudorific.
E.
ष्विद to be unctuous or sweaty, and ल्युट् aff.

f. (-का)
An iron plate or pan used as a cooking utensil.
E.
स्वेदन sweat, ङीष् aff., and कन् fem. form added.

f. (-नी)
An iron plate or pan used as a frying pan, &c.
E.
ष्विद to perspire, ल्युट् and ङीप् affs.

m. (-हः)
A holy or sainted teacher of the Jainas.
E.
स्वेद perspiration, मल excrement, उञ्झित abandoned, and देह body: whose body is no longer subject to its original impurities.

f. (-न्दुः)
A drop of perspiration.
E.
स्वेद, and विन्दु a drop.

f. (-प्रुट्)
A drop of perspiration.
E.
स्वेद sweat, and विप्रुष् a drop.

mfn. (-तः-ता-तं)
Sweated, heated.
E.
स्विद to sweat, causal v., क्त aff.

n. (-कं)
Perspiration.
E.
स्वेद, and उदक water; also स्वेदोद.
